questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to express policy-as-code for security/compliance in multi-cloud clusters, combining network isolation, identity controls, and outbound security.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- NetworkPolicy as runtime guard
- Pod securityContext and automountServiceAccountToken control
- mTLS and central CA validation for outbound traffic
- CI verification using kubectl, gatekeeper audits

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"
        not has_ns_deny_ingress(input)
        msg := "Deployment namespace must have a deny-ingress NetworkPolicy and allow only whitelisted sources."
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no deny ingress and automount enabled)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (deny ingress, trusted SA, automount disabled)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal NetworkPolicy (deny ingress by default, allow from trusted namespace)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

## CI Verification Steps
- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
- kubectl apply -f passing.yaml should succeed and Gatekeeper should record no violations.
- Validate that namespaces have the required NetworkPolicy objects and that deployments use trusted SAs with automountServiceAccountToken disabled.

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical policy design for multi-tenant clusters and how to validate policy with real manifests.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
- image provenance, runtime security, NetworkPolicy, namespace scoping
- validation/testing workflows

## Code Example
```javascript
# ConstraintTemplate.sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
      validation: # omit for brevity
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8ssecurity
      ...
```
```javascript
# Constraint.sample
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-secure-images
spec:
  match:
    kinds: [{apiGroups: ["apps"], kinds: ["Deployment"]}]
  parameters: {registry: "registry.example.com/secure/*"}
```
```javascript
# Compliant Pod/Deployment manifest (snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/secure/app:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        volumeMounts: []
        resources: {requests: {cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi"}, limits: {cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi"}}
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this at scale across 100+ namespaces?
- How would you handle legitimate exceptions or registry migrations?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical policy design, cross-resource validation, and CI integration for multi-tenant clusters. Evaluates trade-offs between strictness and operational overhead.

## Key Concepts

- Kyverno ClusterPolicy for namespace validation
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy egress rules
- Namespace annotations for allowlist
- CI integration: kyverno test, dry-run, and basic egress probe
- Production considerations: DNS allowlists, revocation, and auditing

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-namespace-egress-allowlist
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-egress-annotation
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Namespace
    validate:
      message: "Namespace must declare egress/allowlist annotation"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            egress/allowlist: "*"
  - name: require-egress-networkpolicy
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Namespace
    validate:
      message: "Namespace must have a NetworkPolicy restricting egress"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            networkpolicy/required: "true"
```

- How would you automate rotation of allowlist endpoints in production?
- How would you test for false negatives in CI when a NetworkPolicy is misapplied?

## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

```yaml
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Verification Steps
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify against Gatekeeper policy
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests basic security gating in a beginner-friendly way that ties manifest hardening to CI.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- kube-score risk levels (low/medium/high/critical)
- CI gate integration and failure semantics

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
name: kube-score gate
on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  kube-score:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install kube-score
        run: |
          curl -L -o kube-score https://github.com/zegl/kube-score/releases/download/v1.9.0/kube-score-1.9.0-linux-amd64
          chmod +x kube-score
          sudo mv kube-score /usr/local/bin/kube-score
      - name: Run kube-score
        run: kube-score score manifests/ --output json > kube-score.json
      - name: Fail on high risk
        run: |
          if grep -q high kube-score.json || grep -q critical kube-score.json; then
            echo High-risk issues found
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you scale this to multiple repos?
- How would you handle false positives?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
 Assesses ability to translate security policy into Gatekeeper rules for a multi-tenant cluster.

## Key Concepts
 - Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
 - ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
 - Pod security hardening
 - Kubernetes admission webhook behavior

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate example (high level)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata: {name: K8sContainerHardening}
# ...
```
```yaml
# Constraint example
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sContainerHardeningConstraint
metadata: {name: harden-containers}
spec:
  match: { kinds: [{ apiGroups: [""], kinds: ["Pod"] }] }
  parameters:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    dropCapabilities:
      - ALL
    allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

## Follow-up Questions
 - How would you extend the policy to cover init containers?
 - How would you test with a GitOps workflow and Gatekeeper audit pipeline?
